topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: The Hook: Setting the Stage (45s)
lecture_lines: The Brachistochrone problem seeks the fastest path.
Is it a straight line or a curve?
Gravity dictates the quickest descent for particles.
animations: Show a particle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg] at point A (#FF5733).
Draw a straight path from A to B (#33FF57).
Simulate a particle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg] sliding down the straight path.

sections.title: Defining the Mathematical Landscape (60s)
lecture_lines: Gravity converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
Steeper drops build speed much faster.
Balancing distance and speed is key.
animations: Plot points A (0, 2) and B (2, 0) (#FFFF33) and place a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marble.svg] at point A.
Show the time-to-descent function T(path) (#FFFFFF) while illustrating the path as a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rollercoaster.svg].

sections.title: The Solution: Enter the Cycloid (120s)
lecture_lines: The solution is the unique cycloid curve.
Think of a point on a rolling circle.
The cycloid path optimizes energy conversion.
It steals time to reach high speeds early.
Nature prefers this elegant, efficient trajectory.
animations: Visualize the cycloid curve between A and B (#FF33FF) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg].
Show particle on the cycloid curve (#FF5733) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg].
Compare cycloid descent speed with straight path.
Highlight the cycloid as the fastest path (#00FFFF) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg].

sections.title: The Intuitive 'Why' (45s)
lecture_lines: Straight lines are short but slow initially.
Cycloids start fast, despite a longer path.
The winner balances distance with high velocity.
animations: Illustrate the cycloid's early steep drop using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg] (#FF5733).
Explain how the drop builds velocity early as the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg] descends (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Real-World Significance (30s)
lecture_lines: Variational calculus formally defines this optimal path.
Engineers apply this to roller coaster design.
Optimized curves enhance speed and thrill.
animations: Display a brachistochrone application context involving a thrill ride [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rollercoaster.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the cycloid curve in the application (#FFFF33).
Conclude with the Brachistochrone principle significance for high-speed design [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rollercoaster.svg] (#FFFFFF).
